subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-on threshold-based main-session cron ghost-run warning with run-log/protocol/UI surfacing, as proposed by the linked PR, or require a narrower diagnostic shape?
rationale: Current main still has the source-reproducible fast-ok handoff, but the proposed fix adds operator-visible config and protocol surface that repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Refresh and land the linked diagnostic path
options.body: Resolve the conflicts, settle the config/protocol warning shape, and land the linked PR or a clean replacement for this issue.

options.title: Replace with a narrower warning
options.body: Reject the new config/protocol surface and land a smaller warning or diagnostic that still exposes the silent fast-ok handoff.

options.title: Keep current semantics
options.body: Document that main-session next-heartbeat cron handoff only acknowledges queueing, not agent execution, and close the linked implementation direction.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land the linked diagnostic path
recommendation.body: Resolve the conflicts, settle the config/protocol warning shape, and land the linked PR or a clean replacement for this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is the cron dispatch split in the central timer path, making this the best available routing owner for the product-direction choice.
